sentences.text: Ctenosuchus belongs to the family Teleosauridae, a group of prehistoric crocodile-like reptiles.
This animal is known from two specimens that preserve partial skulls and osteoderms, which are bony plates embedded in the skin.
Fossils of Ctenosuchus have been found in Morocco within the Anoual Formation.
It is a newly described genus and species, established by Imran et al. in 2026.
The species was described by Imran and colleagues, including Hamzah Imran, David M. Martill, and Nizar Ibrahim, and published in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology.
Researchers suggest the interlocking teeth of Ctenosuchus were an adaptation for trapping prey like small crustaceans, fish, and soft-bodied animals.
Ctenosuchus lived during the Middle Jurassic, specifically the Bathonian age.
